raw_response:
I will still do wheat-maize on all 9.5 mu, same as before, because that is what fits my land and water. I do not like changing too much at once. I have well irrigation, so I will push yield a bit, but I still count every bag because 9.5 mu is not small for family labor and cash is always tight. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put the main fertilizer under the land before or at sowing, then chase nitrogen once in spring with water. Around here, if wheat looks weak and I save fertilizer, I lose yield fast, so I would rather keep nitrogen around 15 kg pure nutrient per mu and not let the crop go hungry. I will water wheat about 3 times if the season is normal: one winter or early spring water depending on moisture, one at jointing, and one around heading-filling if it turns dry. For maize, summer time is rushed after wheat harvest, so I will go with hybrid seed and no-tillage or direct seeding into the stubble to save time and labor. I will keep maize fertilizer a little lower than wheat on phosphorus but not low on nitrogen, because if maize loses color in July and August, the ear will shrink and I cannot make that back later. I will spray each crop about 2 times in a normal year, more only if pests become serious. My target is not the top demonstration-field yield; I will aim for a steady, realistic harvest that I can manage with my money and family labor.
